headline: Campground and Astronomy Program Check Required
reservation: Chaco Culture does not require a park entry reservation, but the Gallo Wash Campground frequently reaches capacity months in advance. The park’s popular night sky programs and equinox events involve separate scheduling; verify all logistics via the official NPS portal before navigating the remote access roads. Accommodations outside the park are located in gateway cities like Farmington.

days.title: Architectural Core of the Canyon

stops.name: Pueblo Bonito
stops.detail: Walk through the largest Ancestral Puebloan Great House to observe the precise D-shaped masonry and ancient T-shaped doorways.

stops.name: Chetro Ketl
stops.detail: Explore the extensive plaza and unique elevated kivas of this massive communal structure located a short distance from Pueblo Bonito.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for the journey from Farmington; conditions vary significantly on unpaved sections.
days.note: The final 20 miles of access road are dirt; heavy rain can make these sections impassable for all vehicles.

days.title: Mesa Overlooks and Ancient Paths

stops.name: Pueblo Alto Trail
stops.detail: Ascend the canyon rim for a bird's-eye perspective of the Great House layouts and the prehistoric Chacoan road system.

stops.name: Casa Rinconada
stops.detail: Visit the largest isolated Great Kiva in the park, famous for its symmetrical construction and solar alignments.

days.driving: Minimal driving via the one-way Canyon Loop Drive; allow for slow speeds.
days.note: Trails are highly exposed to sun and wind; carry a minimum of two liters of water per person.

days.title: Outer Ruins and Celestial Heritage

stops.name: Wijiji
stops.detail: Hike or bike the relatively flat trail to this late-period Great House known for its architectural symmetry.

stops.name: Chaco Observatory
stops.detail: Visit the onsite observatory to learn about the park’s status as an International Dark Sky Park.

days.driving: Short distances within the park; allow extra time for potential washboard road conditions.
days.note: Bicycles are permitted only on established roads and the designated Wijiji trail.

intel.title: Unpaved Entrance Roads
intel.text: The park is accessed via New Mexico Highway 57 or County Road 7900; both include rough dirt sections. Check the official park website for current mud or wash-out alerts before leaving paved highways.

intel.title: Remote Services
intel.text: No gasoline or vehicle services are available within the park boundaries. Ensure your tank is full in Bloomfield or Thoreau before beginning the final approach to the canyon.

intel.title: Great House Trailheads
intel.text: Parking at Pueblo Bonito is limited and can be tight during peak spring weekends. Arrive early or consider visiting the less-frequented Hungo Pavi during midday peaks.

intel.title: Cellular Dead Zones
intel.text: Connectivity is non-existent within the canyon and along most of the access roads. Download offline maps and park information at your gateway city before departure.

intel.title: Summer Monsoon Risks
intel.text: Afternoon thunderstorms in July and August can cause flash flooding in the arroyos. Plan all rim hiking for the early morning to avoid lightning and heat exhaustion.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Durango La Plata County Airport, secure groceries and water in Farmington, and allow ample daylight for the final dirt road transition.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are strongly recommended; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved roads.
plan.goldenHour: Pueblo Bonito Overlook via the Pueblo Alto Trail; shadows accentuate masonry textures seasonally.
